newsitem.title: UK: Britain's SFA fines trader for flouting limit rules.
newsitem.headline: Britain's SFA fines trader for flouting limit rules.

text.p: Britain's financial markets regulator the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Thursday it had reprimanded and fined a former trader at Den Danske Bank (DDB for flouting limits on dealings for clients.
Ole Rasmussen, a private banking securities trader, was fined 5,000 pounds ($8,256) and required to pay costs of 4,000.
DDB was also disciplined for the failure of internal controls and fined 15,000 pounds. DDB agreed to pay a contribution towards the SFA's costs of 5,000 pounds.
In 1994 Rasmussen had entered into a number of transactions on behalf of customers without proper instructions from those customers, breaching SFA rules.

The SFA tribunal found that "Mr Rasmussen clearly understood that he was not permitted to undertake discretionary trading" and that his conduct was a "deliberate flouting" of DDB's prohibition against discretionary trading.
Separately, Rasmussen was also found to have undertaken unauthorised personal account dealing between February and July 1994.
Rasmussen's registration with the SFA was suspended in July 1994 when he was dismissed by DDB and investigated by the SFA. He is not currently registered with the SFA.
DDB reported the problems immediately they came to light and assisted fully in its investigation, the SFA said.
